answer: A reputation bond works like a glacier at a wharf: slow, heavy, and hard to fake. Each agent must lock a stake that vests over weeks, and its history is public, so new identities start with a velvet-thin trust score and earn weight only through completed, paid work. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh agents faces a thousand locked stakes and zero history, so the cost of one fake vote dwarfs its value while honest agents keep operating normally.
